text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
LES ECHOS
-- Prime Minister Alain Juppe held a summit meeting on youth unemployment yesterday.
-- EU authorities seek to widen and increase taxes on energy to fend off air pollution.
-- Vallourec to launch joint venture with Mannesmann, Usinor Sacilor to sell its stake in Vallourec.
-- Intel chairman Andy Grove in an interview says that Europe's competitiveness is jeopardised because firms do not invest enough in computers.
-- France Telecom seeks to untie its links with Havas .
-- Broker Dupont Denant to restructure.
LA TRIBUNE
-- The Robien law allowing tax cuts for firms who adopt shorther work weeks to save or create jobs may create up to 500,000 jobs a year, according to OFCE estimates.
-- General Electric will not make engines for Airbus Industrie's planned A340-600 plane.
-- Investors positive on European shares, survey shows.
-- Allianz may be interested in insurer AGF .
L'AGEFI
-- Deutsche Morgan Grenfell seeks to boost its merger and acquisitions activity.
LE FIGARO-ECONOMIE
-- Compagnie de Navigation Mixte sells Via Bourse.
LIBERATION (Economic section)
-- Edouard Stern to bid for bankrupt bank Pallas Stern, Paris court to rule on February 28.
THE INTERNATIONAL HERALD TRIBUNE
-- French on-line business to undergo concentration, only a few major actors with links to telecommunications firms may survive, according to managing director of Hachette Filipacchi Grolier.
